cohort: 105 pregnant women were enrolled, divided into an obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome (OAPS) cohort (n=60) and a control cohort (n=45).
finding: The OAPS cohort showed increased IVRT and MPI and decreased ET, MCA-PI, and CPR compared to controls, and a nomogram based on gravidity, CPR, and MPI accurately predicted adverse perinatal outcomes in OAPS women.
